buildNotes: Every seesaw access is a write of two bytes, module base then function register; for a read wait a few ms, then read the bytes back, big-endian.
Encoder n (0-3) position: base 0x11, register 0x30+n, 4 bytes, signed 32-bit, one count per detent. Register 0x40+n is the delta since the last read.

Knob switches are seesaw GPIO pins 12, 14, 17, 9 (encoders #0-#3): set them input with pull-up (DIRCLR_BULK 0x01 0x03, PULLENSET 0x01 0x0B, BULK_SET 0x01 0x05), then read GPIO_BULK (0x01 0x04, 4 bytes); a bit reads 0 while pressed.
STATUS HW_ID (0x00 0x01) reads 0x87 (ATtiny817); VERSION (0x00 0x02) top 16 bits = 5752.
Default address 0x49; cut A0/A1/A2 on the back to add 1/2/4 (up to 0x50).
No regulator or level shifter: SDA/SCL pull-ups go to VIN, so power VIN from 3.3 V with a 3.3 V board.
Encoders are soldered by you (any PEC11-style encoder); NeoPixels are on seesaw pin 18 (4 pixels, GRB).

driver.code:
# Adafruit I2C Quad Rotary Encoder breakout (product 5752, ATtiny817 running seesaw firmware), MicroPython driver.
# seesaw protocol: every access starts with a write of [module base, function register];
# for a read, wait briefly, then read the bytes back (all values big-endian).
import time

_STATUS_BASE = 0x00
_STATUS_HW_ID = 0x01
_STATUS_VERSION = 0x02
_STATUS_SWRST = 0x7F
_GPIO_BASE = 0x01
_GPIO_DIRCLR_BULK = 0x03
_GPIO_BULK = 0x04
_GPIO_BULK_SET = 0x05
_GPIO_PULLENSET = 0x0B
_NEOPIXEL_BASE = 0x0E
_NEOPIXEL_PIN = 0x01
_NEOPIXEL_SPEED = 0x02
_NEOPIXEL_BUF_LENGTH = 0x03
_NEOPIXEL_BUF = 0x04
_NEOPIXEL_SHOW = 0x05
_ENCODER_BASE = 0x11
_ENCODER_POSITION = 0x30  # + encoder number (0-3)
_ENCODER_DELTA = 0x40     # + encoder number (0-3)

_HW_IDS = (0x55, 0x84, 0x85, 0x86, 0x87, 0x88, 0x89)  # 0x87 = ATtiny817 (this board)
_PRODUCT_ID = 5752
_SWITCH_PINS = (12, 14, 17, 9)  # seesaw pins of the push switches of encoders #0-#3
_NEOPIXEL_SEESAW_PIN = 18
_NUM = 4


class QuadEncoder:
    def __init__(self, i2c, addr=0x49, reset=True):
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = addr
        if reset:
            self._write(_STATUS_BASE, _STATUS_SWRST, b'\xff')
            time.sleep_ms(500)  # seesaw restarts after a software reset
        hw = self._read(_STATUS_BASE, _STATUS_HW_ID, 1)[0]
        if hw not in _HW_IDS:
            raise OSError('seesaw not found at 0x%02x (HW_ID 0x%02x): check the wiring' % (addr, hw))
        v = self._read(_STATUS_BASE, _STATUS_VERSION, 4)
        pid = (v[0] << 8) | v[1]
        if pid != _PRODUCT_ID:
            raise OSError('seesaw at 0x%02x is product %d, not the quad encoder 5752' % (addr, pid))
        # Push switches: inputs with pull-ups (a pressed knob pulls its pin to GND).
        m = 0
        for p in _SWITCH_PINS:
            m |= 1 << p
        mask = m.to_bytes(4, 'big')
        self._write(_GPIO_BASE, _GPIO_DIRCLR_BULK, mask)
        self._write(_GPIO_BASE, _GPIO_PULLENSET, mask)
        self._write(_GPIO_BASE, _GPIO_BULK_SET, mask)
        # NeoPixels: seesaw pin 18, 800 kHz, 4 pixels x 3 bytes (GRB).
        self._write(_NEOPIXEL_BASE, _NEOPIXEL_PIN, bytes([_NEOPIXEL_SEESAW_PIN]))
        self._write(_NEOPIXEL_BASE, _NEOPIXEL_SPEED, b'\x01')
        self._write(_NEOPIXEL_BASE, _NEOPIXEL_BUF_LENGTH, (_NUM * 3).to_bytes(2, 'big'))

    def _write(self, base, reg, data=b''):
        self.i2c.writeto(self.addr, bytes([base, reg]) + bytes(data))

    def _read(self, base, reg, n, delay_us=8000):
        self.i2c.writeto(self.addr, bytes([base, reg]))
        time.sleep_us(delay_us)  # seesaw needs time to fetch the value before the read
        return self.i2c.readfrom(self.addr, n)

    @staticmethod
    def _int32(b):
        v = (b[0] << 24) | (b[1] << 16) | (b[2] << 8) | b[3]
        return v - (1 << 32) if v & 0x80000000 else v

    @staticmethod
    def _check(n):
        if not 0 <= n < _NUM:
            raise IndexError('encoder number 0-3')

    def position(self, n=0):
        """Position of encoder n (0-3) in detents (signed 32-bit counter kept by seesaw)."""
        self._check(n)
        return self._int32(self._read(_ENCODER_BASE, _ENCODER_POSITION + n, 4))

    def positions(self):
        return [self.position(n) for n in range(_NUM)]

    def set_position(self, n, pos):
        self._check(n)
        self._write(_ENCODER_BASE, _ENCODER_POSITION + n, (pos & 0xFFFFFFFF).to_bytes(4, 'big'))

    def delta(self, n=0):
        """Detents encoder n turned since its last delta() read (reading clears it)."""
        self._check(n)
        return self._int32(self._read(_ENCODER_BASE, _ENCODER_DELTA + n, 4))

    def _gpio(self):
        b = self._read(_GPIO_BASE, _GPIO_BULK, 4)
        return (b[0] << 24) | (b[1] << 16) | (b[2] << 8) | b[3]

    def pressed(self, n=0):
        """True while knob n (0-3) is pushed in."""
        self._check(n)
        return not (self._gpio() >> _SWITCH_PINS[n]) & 1

    def pressed_all(self):
        bits = self._gpio()
        return [not (bits >> p) & 1 for p in _SWITCH_PINS]

    def pixel(self, n, r, g, b, show=True):
        """Set the NeoPixel under encoder n (0-3) to r, g, b (0-255 each)."""
        self._check(n)
        self._write(_NEOPIXEL_BASE, _NEOPIXEL_BUF, (n * 3).to_bytes(2, 'big') + bytes([g & 255, r & 255, b & 255]))
        if show:
            self.show()

    def show(self):
        self._write(_NEOPIXEL_BASE, _NEOPIXEL_SHOW)

# Adafruit I2C Quad Rotary Encoder (Adafruit 5752)

## Overview
Four rotary encoders with push switches, read over I2C. An **ATtiny817** running Adafruit's **seesaw** firmware counts the detents of each encoder in its own signed 32-bit position and reads the four knob switches, so the whole board needs only SDA and SCL. There is a NeoPixel under each knob (seesaw pin 18, 4 pixels), two STEMMA QT / Qwiic sockets and an INT output. You solder the four encoders yourself (any PEC11-style encoder, with or without a switch).

## Pinout (header order, as printed on the board)
The 6-pad header appears twice (top and bottom edge, same signals). Left to right:

| Pin | Function |
|---|---|
| VIN | Supply, 3-5 V. It is also the I2C logic level, so use your board's logic voltage |
| - | Ground |
| C | I2C clock SCL (10 k pull-up to VIN on board) |
| D | I2C data SDA (10 k pull-up to VIN on board) |
| INT | Interrupt output, pulses low on a turn or press (only when enabled in seesaw) |
| UPDI | Unlabelled pad: ATtiny817 programming pin, leave unconnected |

## Electrical limits
- Supply: 3-5 V on VIN (ATtiny817 runs straight from VIN; no regulator or level shifter).
- The SDA/SCL pull-ups go to VIN. On a 3.3 V board (ESP32, Pico, Raspberry Pi) power it from **3.3 V**, never 5 V, or the I2C lines are pulled to 5 V.
- Current: a few mA, plus up to about 20 mA per NeoPixel at full white.

## Interface details
- **I2C address 0x49** by default. Cutting the A0/A1/A2 jumpers on the back adds 1/2/4 (up to 0x50).
- seesaw protocol: write `[module base, function register]` plus any data. To read, write the two bytes, wait (the driver waits 8 ms), then read. Values are big-endian.
- STATUS base 0x00: HW_ID 0x01 reads **0x87** (ATtiny817). VERSION 0x02 (4 bytes): the top 16 bits are the product number, **5752**. SWRST 0x7F: write 0xFF, then wait about 500 ms.
- ENCODER base 0x11: POSITION is register **0x30 + n** for encoder n (0-3), a signed 32-bit count of detents (writable). DELTA is **0x40 + n**, cleared on read.
- Switches: seesaw GPIO pins **12, 14, 17, 9** for encoders #0, #1, #2, #3. Set them as inputs with pull-ups (DIRCLR_BULK 0x01 0x03, PULLENSET 0x01 0x0B, BULK_SET 0x01 0x05 with the pin mask), then read GPIO_BULK (0x01 0x04, 4 bytes). A bit reads 0 while that knob is pressed.

## Wiring
- ESP32: VIN → 3V3, - → GND, D → D21, C → D22.
- Pico: VIN → 3V3(OUT), - → GND, D → GP4, C → GP5.
- Raspberry Pi 4: VIN → pin 1 (3.3 V), - → pin 6, D → pin 3, C → pin 5.
- Or use a STEMMA QT / Qwiic cable.

## Using the driver
```python
from machine import I2C, Pin
from seesaw_quad_encoder import QuadEncoder
i2c = I2C(0, sda=Pin(21), scl=Pin(22))
q = QuadEncoder(i2c)                 # address 0x49
print(q.positions(), q.pressed_all())
q.pixel(0, 0, 40, 0)                 # green under knob #0
```

## Gotchas
- Always leave a short delay between the register write and the read.
- Encoder #3's switch is seesaw pin 9 (per Adafruit's own examples and library); the learn guide's encoder #0 B-pin listing also shows 9, which is a typo there.
- Direction: Adafruit's example negates position to make clockwise positive. Flip the sign if needed.
- In the Sparkbench simulator the sliders set each POSITION register; DELTA is not modelled, so use `position()` there.
- Driver raises OSError if the seesaw at that address is not product 5752 (e.g. a single-encoder board at 0x36).

## Datasheet
- ATtiny817 (the chip): https://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/en/DeviceDoc/ATtiny417-814-816-817-DataSheet-DS40002288A.pdf
- Board guide: https://learn.adafruit.com/adafruit-i2c-quad-rotary-encoder-breakout

from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from seesaw_quad_encoder import QuadEncoder

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
q = QuadEncoder(i2c)
while True:
    p = q.positions()
    s = q.pressed_all()
    print('pos=%d,%d,%d,%d sw=%s' % (p[0], p[1], p[2], p[3], ''.join('1' if b else '0' for b in s)))
    time.sleep_ms(200)
